title: Chapter 5 Problem Set: Concurrent Bank Ledger & Order Actor (ledger_actor.erl)
solutionExplanation: Implements an in-memory concurrent banking ledger actor with tail-recursive loop, atomic deposit/withdraw/transfer, and dual-accumulator batch execution.

otpDocCards.description: Creates a concurrent process with its own private heap and returns its unique PID.
Returns an almost unique reference token used for request-reply correlation.

mentalModelCheck.question: Why is an in-memory Erlang ledger actor immune to double-spend race conditions even when 1,000 concurrent client processes attempt to withdraw the same $100 balance simultaneously?
mentalModelCheck.codeSnippet:
%% 1,000 client processes blasting simultaneous withdrawals:
[spawn(fun() -> ledger_actor:process_transaction(Ledger, {withdraw, 1, 100}) end)
 || _ <- lists:seq(1, 1000)].

options.label: The ledger actor process serializes all incoming withdrawal messages sequentially through its private mailbox, processing one transaction at a time and updating its state before inspecting the next message.
options.explanation: Correct! The Actor Model eliminates race conditions through sequential mailbox processing. Even if 1,000 messages arrive at the same microsecond, they queue up in the mailbox and are handled one at a time.

options.label: Erlang uses Linux kernel hardware locks to freeze RAM addresses.
options.explanation: Erlang does not use hardware memory locks; state is isolated to the process heap.

options.label: The compiler converts concurrent withdrawals into SQL transactions.
options.explanation: Erlang actor state is purely in-memory; no SQL database is involved.
